Bug described: urlize does not handle html escaped string and trailing punctuation correctly. The example shows input 'Search for google.com/?q=1<! and see.' expected output includes link with href http://google.com/... and text "google.com/?q=1lt" then exclamation after link. Actual output had '...google.com/?q=1<lt!'. So bug: when input contains escaped '<' entity, the algorithm incorrectly splits punctuation. Specifically, word_split_re splits on whitespace and <>"', so it splits at '<' causing issue. The code uses html.unescape(middle) before smart_urlquote but then later escape(lead), escape(trail). But for escaped '<', middle is 'google.com/?q=1<'. After trim_punctuation, lead/trail? Let's analyze: word contains 'google.com/?q=1<!'. In loop, lead='', middle='google.com/?q=1<!', trail='' initially. trim_punctuation will strip trailing punctuation after unescaping; html.unescape('google.com/?q=1<!') => 'google.com/?q=1<', then rstrip(TRAILING_PUNCTUATION_CHARS) removes '!'? Actually TRAILING includes '!'. So stripped becomes 'google.com/?q=1<' . Then trail = middle[len(stripped):] + trail -> original middle len 20? Let's compute: middle='google.com/?q=1<!'; stripped='google.com/?q=1<'; length difference 1 char '!' removed. trail becomes '!' + '' => '!'. middle set to stripped[:len(stripped)-len(middle_unescaped)]? Specifically, after unescape, middle_unescaped='google.com/?q=1<', stripped same. len(stripped)=... len(middle_unescaped)=... difference 0 so middle becomes empty? That leads to link text missing 'lt'. That's why output shows only '<' part. So bug is in trim_punctuation logic: line 287 incorrectly uses len(stripped) - len(middle_unescaped). Should be len(middle) - len(stripped)? Let's compute: original middle length 20, stripped length maybe 19? Actually 'google.com/?q=1<': length 18? Wait count. But anyway. Simpler: modify trim_punctuation to handle entities properly by not altering the escaped part incorrectly. The bug arises because after unescape, stripped may be shorter than middle_unescaped due to removal of '!' but then middle set to empty. Should instead compute difference between original middle length and stripped length? Actually we want to keep entity part '<' which is encoded as '<' originally; after unescape becomes '<', so we should keep that in middle.
